subject: Culture
title: Turning of the Bones
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Turning of the Bones.

hook.text: In Madagascar, families dig up their dead, wrap them in fresh cloth, and dance with the corpses in a joyful reunion.

buildup.text: The ritual, called 'famadihana,' happens every five to seven years. It's the most important social event in the area.

discovery.text: The Malagasy believe the dead are not truly gone until everyone who remembers them has also died.

twist.text: The ceremony costs months of savings. Families go into debt because honoring ancestors is worth more than comfort.

climax.text: Health officials worry about disease exposure. But banning the ritual would sever the community's deepest bond.

punchline.text: Some bonds don't end at the grave—they visit it.

quiz.question: How often is 'famadihana' performed in Madagascar?
